findings.text: _extract_error_lint_ids re-states the one-line lint-summary format f"[{severity}:lint:{finding_type}] {name_id}: {detail[:200]}" verbatim from _extract_audit_findings (pipeline.py:1752-1756), so the string the reviewer is shown and the string the cap records are maintained in two places; a change to one leaves the prompt and the recorded audit_cap_finding to drift, where a shared one-line-summary helper would give that format a single owner.

test_audit_findings_block_is_absent_when_no_findings (line 52) renders with audit_findings=[] and asserts FINDING_MARKER (line 65) is absent, but FINDING_MARKER is a literal only ever supplied by the sibling render test, so no renderer could emit it regardless of the template's if-guard; the assertion names no code change under which it reddens and does not guard the {% if audit_findings %} condition it claims to test.

the cap skips any entry whose score is already below DEFAULT_MIN_SCORE and records nothing (line 1957), so an entry that holds an error-severity lint finding but was independently scored below acceptance carries neither audit_cap_applied nor audit_cap_finding; the plan asks each scored entry among the error-holding names to record that the cap applied and which finding caused it, and here the finding is dropped from the record even though it stands.

the second documentation call site, _review_batch_core, calls _review_single_batch with audit_findings=[] and no error_lint_findings, so the cap cannot fire and the findings block cannot render on that path; it is reached only by tests today (loop.py imports process_review_docs_batch from workers.py, not pipeline.py), so it is recorded rather than blocking, but extending the render/cap into _review_single_batch leaves this sibling docs path uncapped.
